jobs.occupation: Sales Oriented Business Manager to ALTEN Denmark
jobs.description:
Would you like to work in a varied role with a focus on sales, recruitment and leadership? Then we have the position for you! ALTEN Group is seeking to appoint a Business Manager with the aim to develop our business to the Danish market. 
 
As Business Manager, you will be responsible for establishing and developing the ALTEN organization in Denmark where you will report directly to the Managing Director of Sweden. 

To be considered for the role as Business Manager, you are required to have a master degree within engineering or business as well as 3 to 5 years’ relevant experience of working within sales and/or recruitment. Furthermore, you are fluent in both Danish and English, spoken as well as written. Experience of the IT or Technology consultancy business is meritorious. 

As a person, you are committed with a strong interest in sales and business development. You appreciate challenges and have a goal-oriented mindset. You prefer working in a fast-paced and inconstant environment. In addition to this, you are good at establishing and maintaining relationships with other people.

The position is located in Copenhagen but frequent travel will occur, both nationally and internationally. Your main responsibilities as Business Manager are: 
- Prospection and sales towards new and existent clients
- Managing the entire recruitment process, from need to hiring
- Managing the group of consultants you have hired 
- Coaching, support and career development of your consultants 
- Producing accurate business forecasts and reports for your Business Unit
- Budget responsibility for your Business Unit About ALTEN Group
With over 30 000 employees in 22 countries, we develop and deliver competence for world leading companies through the most committed engineering and IT consultants. Our customers are found in industries such as Energy, Telecom, Automotive, Defence & Aerospace and Life Science and we are active throughout the whole product lifecycle. We offer you an interesting role in an international environment with a clearly defined career ladder for your own development. As Business Manager, you also have both international and national educations as well as regular coaching.

 UCG/Radio Support is a consulting company based in Kista in northern Stockholm. Regardless placement you will be employed by UCG, with Swedish salary and benifits.  

The Consultant roll 
As a consultant you may be placed at different customers. UCG will assist with extra training when needed. As a consultant we need you to be flexible and to easily adapt to a new environment.

The company
The ILL is an international research facility at the forefront of neutron science and technology. Its High-Flux Nuclear Reactor delivers the world's most intense neutron beams to a suite of over 40 scientific instruments. Every year, some 1800 international researchers visit the ILL to carry out cutting-edge experiments across a range of scientific disciplines, driving innovation in the fields of health, energy, the environment and quantum materials. The ILL is also involved in the production of radioisotopes for medical applications. The ILL employs over 500 staff from 25 different countries, in a diversity of careers and a multicultural and inclusive environment.

The Science Division at ILL brings together close to 200 scientists, engineers, and technicians who work collaboratively to provide users with advanced experimental capabilities and expert scientific support. The DS is responsible by operating world-class neutron scattering instruments, supporting an international user community, conducting cutting-edge research, and developing new experimental techniques. In addition, the division drives the development of next-generation instrumentation and computational tools, fosters international collaborations, and contributes to advanced training.

About the position
As an experiment support and instrument technician, you will be responsible for the operation and development of experimental equipment and for providing support for experiments conducted at the ILL.
You will work closely with the scientists in charge of the instruments you will be assigned to. You will also collaborate with the other technicians in the Spectroscopy group. You will act as technical contact for the instrument WASP within this group. Depending on the needs of the different groups, you may be asked to work in parallel on other instruments within the Spectroscopy group.

Your tasks
Your main duties will involve the following:
-    Performing maintenance work and repairs on instruments and their ancillary equipment
-    Assisting in-house and visiting scientists with the preparation of their experiments
-    Designing new equipment in collaboration with ILL scientists and technical support groups
-    Improving the instruments and the way in which experiments are conducted by devising innovative technical solutions
-    Performing precision machining of simple mechanical parts (lathing, milling, drilling) at short notice
-    Installing, maintaining and operating sample environment equipment (cryostats, furnaces, etc.)
-    Organising the purchase of new equipment and spare parts

Desired profile
-    You have a Level 4/5 qualification (e.g. NVQ, BTEC HNC/HND or equivalent) in mechanical, maintenance or electronic engineering.
-    You have experience in the assembly and alignment of precision mechanical assemblies.
-    You have knowledge of CAD software.
-    Experience in scientific instrumentation, in particular in the field of cryogenics, would be an advantage.
-    You must have a sound knowledge of English and be willing to learn French (a language course will be paid for by the ILL).

Benefits
Quality of life - This position is based in Grenoble, a hub for research and technology, ideally located in the heart of the French Alps (just 3 hours from Paris/Provence by train, 1 hour from Lyon international airport and 1 ½ hours from Geneva). It is important for us that our staff achieve a healthy work-life balance. We therefore offer home working (under certain conditions), generous annual paid leave entitlement and a host of other benefits that you will discover when you arrive!

Prospects - We guarantee you a secure permanent position based in Grenoble in a multicultural scientific environment.

Benefits - We offer generous social benefits (expatriation allowance, excellent health cover), moving and relocation assistance (under certain conditions) and an annual productivity bonus. We also offer language courses for you and your partner and subsidies for the use of public transport and the staff canteen, as well as for holidays and a variety of cultural and sports activities. For more details, visit https://www.ill.eu/careers/working-at-the-ill/employment-conditions.

jobs.description:
Context
The Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL), situated in Grenoble, France, is Europe's leading research facility for scientific research using neutrons. Every year, we host over 2000 visits by scientists, who come to the Institute to carry out world-class research.
Within the Industrial Liaison Unit (ILU, 2 people) of ILL's Applied Science Group (18 people), you will act as an effective and efficient interface between industry and the cutting-edge neutron techniques and scientists available at the ILL for proprietary research and development (R&D) as well as non-destructive testing (NDT).

Your tasks
In this context, you will:
. Organise and perform efficient and successful proprietary R&D and NDT utilising ILL's neutron instruments, working closely with instrument scientists and industry clients.
. Build up expertise in neutron techniques and operating instruments relevant to industrial R&D and NDT opportunities.
. Contribute to a strategy to increase industrial R&D and NDT activity at ILL, to maximise revenue from this activity (currently around 0.5 M? per year).
. Undertake outreach and communication activities for industrial R&D/NDT at ILL to build up a portfolio of high-potential industry contacts and generate new business opportunities.
. Manage the customer base and maintain an accurate record of all industry-related activities at ILL for periodic reporting and review for optimisation of ILL's industry strategy with Management.
. With support from the legal service at ILL, organise the contractual agreements for proprietary beam time.
. With ILL's Grants Office, your line manager and relevant ILL scientists, identify and pursue project-based opportunities for industry-related research at ILL.
. Liaise with local, regional and international partners to nurture a robust, collective approach to industry services at large-scale research facilities.

Your profile
. You hold a PhD in engineering or a natural science (or equivalent qualification) and have several years of experience in a range of analytical techniques, preferably using neutrons.
. You have excellent communication skills, are highly interested in applied research and have some experience in working with industry / R&D / NDT.
. You have a strong project management culture, which will enable you to plan and manage the ILL's involvement in R&D and NDT with industry partners.

What we offer
Quality of life - This position is based in Grenoble, a hub for research and technology, ideally located in the heart of the French Alps (just 3 hours from Paris/Provence by train, 1 hour from Lyon international airport and 1 ½ hours from Geneva). It is important for us that our staff achieve a healthy work-life balance. We therefore offer home working (under certain conditions), generous annual paid leave entitlement and a host of other benefits that you will discover when you arrive!

Prospects - We guarantee you a stable 5-year fixed-term contract position in a multicultural scientific environment.

Benefits - We offer generous social benefits (expatriation allowance, excellent health cover), moving and relocation assistance (under certain conditions) and an annual productivity bonus. We also offer language courses for you and your partner and subsidies for the use of public transport and the staff canteen, as well as for holidays and a variety of cultural and sports activities. For more details, visit https://www.ill.eu/careers/working-at-the-ill/employment-conditions

Sounds interesting?
Then why not take your next career step with us by applying online - preferably in English - via our career portal by 11.10.2026, quoting reference number 26/40 Please note that all applicants are subject to administrative screening (background checks). For this post, medical fitness, including for work under ionising radiation, is required.

We are committed to equal opportunities and diversity and therefore welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates.

Core mission
The Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL), situated in Grenoble, France, is Europe's leading research facility for scientific research using neutrons. Every year we host over 2000 visits by scientists, who come to the Institute to carry out world-class research.
You will join the ILL's Reactor Division, where you will perform secretarial duties for the Head of Division and provide general administrative support to the entire division. This role is at the heart of the ILL's relations with France's nuclear safety and security authorities. It calls for a meticulous approach to the handling of sensitive documents and involves working in close collaboration with the personal assistants of the other members of the ILL's Management Board. Special security clearance ('habilitation') is required for this post, given the sensitive nature of some of the documents and activities associated with the role.

Your tasks
. Handle administrative relations with the French authorities (French nuclear safety authority (ASNR), Senior Defence and Security Advisor (HFDS) within the Ministry of Ecological Transition and its technical support services, Préfecture, police): processing, distributing and archiving incoming and outgoing correspondence, maintaining the correspondence register.
. Manage the logistics involved with inspections (ASNR, HFDS, EURATOM) and emergency response exercises.
. Handle documents classified as "Secret" and "Restricted" and monitor compliance with the associated security clearance and screening procedures.
. Handle administrative matters linked to crisis management: badges for access to CEA Grenoble, maintaining the list of ILL staff who may be involved and the associated documentation.
. Remain up to date with safety reference frameworks (safety report, general operating rules, on-site emergency plan and safety instruction sheets) and regulatory documents relating to nuclear materials, as well as documents governing reactor operations (procedures, RHF reactor reports, instructions).
. Organise regular meetings of the Reactor Division and draft the associated minutes.
. Organise important visits to the Reactor Division (safety authorities, public authorities) and other events, in collaboration with the other personal assistants.
. Perform secretarial duties for the Head of the Reactor Division: managing his agenda, phone calls, emails, correspondence, travel arrangements and travel expenses.
. Coordinate the annual performance reviews and manage data forwarded to the Joint Careers Commission.
. Collaborate with the personal assistants of the other members of the Management Board to ensure that actions are effectively coordinated in line with the objectives set.

our profile
. Level 4/5 qualification in business and administration or a related field, or administrative secretary and personal assistant diploma
. Proven experience as a personal assistant
. Excellent command of written and spoken English and French
. Meticulous nature and professionalism, particularly in the handling of sensitive and/or classified documents
. Strong organisational skills, ability to manage a variety of tasks simultaneously and liaise with multiple stakeholders
. Ability to perform day-to-day tasks independently
. Good interpersonal and teamwork skills, particularly when coordinating with the other personal assistants.

What we offer
Quality of life - This position is based in Grenoble, a hub for research and technology, ideally located in the heart of the French Alps (just 3 hours from Paris/Provence by train, 1 hour from Lyon international airport and 1 ½ hours from Geneva). It is important for us that our staff achieve a healthy work-life balance. We therefore offer home working (under certain conditions), generous annual paid leave entitlement and a host of other benefits that you will discover when you arrive!

Prospects - We guarantee you a secure permanent position based in Grenoble in a multicultural scientific environment.

Benefits - We offer generous social benefits (expatriation allowance, excellent health cover), moving and relocation assistance (under certain conditions) and an annual productivity bonus. We also offer language courses for you and your partner and subsidies for the use of public transport and the staff canteen, as well as for holidays and a variety of cultural and sports activities. For more details, visit https://www.ill.eu/careers/working-at-the-ill/employment-conditions.

Sounds interesting?
Then why not take your next career step with us by applying online - preferably in English - via our career portal by 04/10/2026, quoting reference number 26/39. Please note that all applicants are subject to administrative screening (background checks). For this post, medical fitness (including for work under ionising radiation) is required. We are committed to equal opportunities and diversity and therefore welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates.
